content_metadata.description: A detailed tutorial by Genesis Rider, explaining the functions and usage of the Xbox One audio adapter with insights into addressing double audio issues and utilizing the volume mixing feature.

qAndA.answer: The issue is hearing double game audio when using a headset with the Xbox One audio adapter.
qAndA.question: What is the issue that Genesis Rider is addressing in the video?

qAndA.answer: The adapter has two buttons on the side with plus and minus icons for increasing or decreasing either chat or game volume independently.
qAndA.question: How does the adapter allow users to adjust the mix between chat and game audio?

qAndA.answer: Holding down the plus button with the person icon increases chat volume and decreases game volume.
qAndA.question: What does the plus button on the side of the adapter do when held down?

qAndA.answer: He suggests plugging in regular earphones and using it for game audio only, particularly for late-night gaming.
qAndA.question: What other use does Genesis Rider suggest for the adapter besides chat audio?

qAndA.answer: Both devices have similar functionality in terms of mixing game and chat audio, with dedicated controls for adjusting the balance between the two sources.
qAndA.question: How does the Astro A40 MixAmp compare to the Xbox One audio adapter?

youtube_description:
A detailed explanation of the different button functions on the face of the "Xbox One Stereo Headset Adapter." This small device snaps into the base of your controller & provides both game & chat audio to your headset. This video will show you how to balance both game & chat audio as well as fix the annoying "doubled game sound" issue.

IMPORTANT UPDATE: If you own a newer Xbox One controller with an already built in 3.5mm audio jack you don't need this adapter as everything the adapter does is already built into your controller! Simply plug your earphones into your controller, double-tap the home button and scroll down to your settings "gear" icon to modify your volume options. Hope this helps! :)
